name: Kitan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: extinct; known only from Kitan scripts (Kane 2009 treats script/lexicon); stress unrecoverable

sources.note: Nothing. The phonology material is Ch. 1, sections 1.30-1.38 (pp. 28-33: phonograms, graphs for vowels, VV/VC/CV syllable types, vowel harmony, inherent vowels, multiple readings); read in full, and a grep of the entire text layer finds 'accent' only as a diacritic ('acute accent', 'accented letters') and no occurrence of stress/prosody/suprasegmental. Kane states the transcriptions are 'no more than plausible possibilities' (p. 33) and that systematic normalisation is premature.
No phonology or stress content; cites Janhunen 2006 (Para-Mongolic, in The Mongolic Languages, Routledge), Vovin 2017 (AOH 70/2) and Kane 2009.
